scope: Verification-only composition of A1 machine identity, A2 authority manifest, optional A3a attenuation proof, and A4a signed handoff. It emits a content-addressed verification report but creates no identity, authority, signature, delegation, handoff, effect, or network action.
core_invariant: Successful artifact verification proves only the integrity and cross-binding properties explicitly checked. It does not turn historical/snapshot evidence into current authority, execution permission, delegation authority, task success, effect execution, legal identity, or truth.

risks: pair valid artifacts from different principals or snapshots
controls: A2 independently reproduces A1 principal/credential binding
A4 independently verifies A1+A2 binding
verification report binds exact component digests
A4 expected-recipient/executor/identity/input/parent checks are exposed through A10a
report binds exact target and input fields

risks: A3a proof interpreted as proof parent had delegation authority
proof attached to A4a as delegation chain
synthetic positive attenuation treated as runtime delegation
controls: A3a verification is optional and separately labeled proof_only
report keeps delegation_authority_verified=false
A4a delegation_chain_head_digest must remain null

risks: integrity report changed to execution authorization
controls: closed fixed claims
claims validated before report digest acceptance
content-addressed report digest
authority_effect=none

risks: verification tool signs or creates authority artifacts
controls: verification module imports only canonical and verify primitives
static regression forbids node:crypto/fs/child_process/net/http/https imports and creation/sign/effect APIs

risks: historical A1/A2/A4 validity treated as globally current
absence of A6 revocation oracle treated as active authority
controls: global_currentness_verified=false
revocation_currentness_verified=false
authority_granted=false
execution_authorized=false

risks: same-repository composition described as a fully independent third-party implementation
conformance bundle marketed as vendor-neutral interoperability proof
controls: A10a is explicitly a verification bundle using canonical AXIOM verifier primitives
separate implementation/runtime and cross-vendor conformance remain later A10/A9 gates

known_nonclaims: A10a is not a separately implemented third-party verifier; it is a verification-only bundle composed from canonical AXIOM verifier primitives.
A10a does not verify A5 portable work receipts yet.
A10a does not establish live revocation/currentness or delegation authority.
A10a does not authorize or execute the A4 handoff.
A10a does not prove legal identity, task success, effect execution, application correctness, or truth.
A10a does not expose an MCP/A2A/network endpoint or modify capability-registry state.
next_gates: A10b extend the bundle to green A5 portable work receipts once A5a is validated
A10c package a runtime-separated verifier fixture/process with only public verification inputs
A9 adapter parity fixtures proving identical native/MCP/A2A authorization semantics
third-party or independently implemented conformance harness before any universal-agent-trust claim
